# pizza_analysis

Import data

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

df = pd.read_excel("Enhanced_pizza_sell_data_2024-25.xlsx")

print(df.head())
print(df.columns)
```


## Section 1 — Customer Segmentation & Preferences

This section analyzes customer ordering preferences, including pizza type popularity, size preference by time, and weekend vs. weekday behavior.


### 1.1 Most Popular Pizza Types

```{python}
pizza_type_counts = df["Pizza Type"].value_counts()

print("Most Popular Pizza Types:")
print(pizza_type_counts)

plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.barplot(x=pizza_type_counts.index, y=pizza_type_counts.values)
plt.title("Most Popular Pizza Types")
plt.xlabel("Pizza Type")
plt.ylabel("Number of Orders")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

Non-Veg pizzas were the most popular category, followed closely by Veg and Cheese Burst pizzas.

Traditional specialty pizzas such as Deep Dish and Thin Crust had significantly lower demand, suggesting limited customer preference in this dataset.

The strong performance of Veg and Vegan pizzas may indicate increasing demand for vegetarian alternatives.




### 1.2 Pizza Size Preference by Time of Day

```{python}
size_by_hour = pd.crosstab(df["Order Hour"], df["Pizza Size"])

print(size_by_hour)

size_by_hour.plot(kind="bar", figsize=(12,6))
plt.title("Pizza Size Preference by Order Hour")
plt.xlabel("Order Hour")
plt.ylabel("Number of Orders")
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

Pizza size preference varied significantly by order hour.

Medium pizzas dominated during early dinner hours, especially around 18:00 and 20:00, suggesting that medium-sized orders are the most common for regular meal consumption.

At 19:00, Large and XL pizzas sharply increased, indicating that customers may place larger group or family orders during peak dinner time.

Small pizzas had relatively low demand throughout the day, while XL pizzas were concentrated mainly during the busiest evening period.




### 1.3 Weekend vs Weekday Ordering Behavior

```{python}
weekend_behavior = df.groupby("Is Weekend").agg({
    "Toppings Count": "mean",
    "Pizza Complexity": "mean",
    "Delivery Duration (min)": "mean",
    "Order ID": "count"
}).rename(columns={"Order ID": "Order Count"})

print(weekend_behavior)

sns.boxplot(x="Is Weekend", y="Pizza Complexity", data=df)
plt.title("Pizza Complexity: Weekend vs Weekday")
plt.show()
```


### Business Insight

Weekday orders accounted for the majority of total transactions, with 718 orders compared to 286 weekend orders.

Weekday orders also showed slightly higher average toppings count and pizza complexity, suggesting that customers may place more customized or complex orders during weekdays.

However, average delivery duration remained very similar between weekdays and weekends, indicating that operational performance stayed relatively stable across different days of the week.

The boxplot further shows that pizza complexity distributions were relatively similar for both weekday and weekend orders, although weekday orders demonstrated slightly higher median complexity.





## Section 2 — Pricing & Value Perception

This dataset does not contain actual price, revenue, or order amount variables. Therefore, this section uses pizza size, toppings count, and pizza complexity as proxy variables for customer value perception.

### 2.1 Do Larger or More Complex Pizzas Lead to Longer Delays?

```{python}
size_delay = df.groupby("Pizza Size").agg({
    "Delay (min)": "mean",
    "Delivery Duration (min)": "mean",
    "Pizza Complexity": "mean",
    "Order ID": "count"
}).rename(columns={"Order ID": "Order Count"})

print(size_delay)

sns.barplot(x="Pizza Size", y="Delay (min)", data=df)
plt.title("Average Delay by Pizza Size")
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

Pizza size showed a strong relationship with delivery duration, delay, and pizza complexity.

Small pizzas had the shortest average delivery duration and lowest delay, indicating that simpler orders are easier and faster to prepare and deliver.

Large and XL pizzas required significantly longer delivery times, which may be associated with higher preparation complexity and operational workload.

XL pizzas had the highest pizza complexity score, suggesting that larger orders often involve more ingredients, customization, or group-order behavior.

Medium pizzas represented the highest order volume, making them the dominant product category in the dataset.


```{python}
complexity_corr = df[[
    "Pizza Complexity",
    "Toppings Count",
    "Topping Density",
    "Delivery Duration (min)",
    "Delay (min)"
]].corr()

print(complexity_corr)

sns.heatmap(complexity_corr, annot=True, cmap="Blues")
plt.title("Complexity, Toppings, Delivery Time, and Delay Correlation")
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

Pizza Complexity and Toppings Count showed a very strong positive correlation (0.96), indicating that pizzas with more toppings are substantially more operationally complex.

Delivery Duration and Delay also demonstrated a strong positive correlation (0.88), suggesting that longer delivery processes significantly increase the probability of delays.

Pizza Complexity and Toppings Count both showed moderate positive relationships with Delivery Duration, indicating that highly customized orders require more operational effort and delivery time.

Interestingly, Topping Density showed a moderate negative correlation with both Delivery Duration and Delay. This may indicate that smaller pizzas with dense toppings can still be prepared and delivered relatively efficiently.





### 2.2 Toppings Count / Density and Delivery Time

```{python}
sns.scatterplot(
    x="Toppings Count",
    y="Delivery Duration (min)",
    data=df
)

plt.title("Toppings Count vs Delivery Duration")
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

The scatter plot suggests a positive relationship between Toppings Count and Delivery Duration.

Orders with a larger number of toppings generally required longer delivery times, likely due to increased preparation complexity and operational workload.

Higher topping counts also showed greater variability in delivery duration, indicating that highly customized orders may introduce operational inconsistency and delivery uncertainty.


```{python}
sns.scatterplot(
    x="Topping Density",
    y="Delivery Duration (min)",
    data=df
)

plt.title("Topping Density vs Delivery Duration")
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

The scatter plot indicates a moderate negative relationship between Topping Density and Delivery Duration.

Orders with higher topping density generally showed shorter delivery durations. This may occur because smaller pizzas can have relatively high topping density while still requiring less preparation and transportation time.

This finding suggests that total operational complexity and pizza size may influence delivery duration more strongly than topping density alone.





### 2.3 Payment Method and Order Size

```{python}
payment_size = pd.crosstab(df["Payment Method"], df["Pizza Size"])

print(payment_size)

payment_size.plot(kind="bar", figsize=(10,6))
plt.title("Payment Method vs Pizza Size")
plt.xlabel("Payment Method")
plt.ylabel("Number of Orders")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()
```

### Business Insight

Medium pizzas were the most frequently ordered size across nearly all payment methods, confirming that medium-sized pizzas represent the dominant customer preference.

Card and UPI payments showed relatively higher proportions of Large and XL pizza orders, suggesting that digital payment users may be associated with larger or group-based purchases.

Cash payments demonstrated a stronger preference for Small pizzas compared to digital payment methods, which may indicate lower-value or individual orders.

Wallet payments also showed strong Medium pizza demand, suggesting that digital wallet promotions may be particularly effective for medium-sized pizza campaigns.

Loyalty-based payment methods such as Hut Points and Domino's Cash represented only a small proportion of total transactions, indicating relatively limited usage in this dataset.
